# WR-obs-exp1 — Observation Primitive: FNV-1a Canary Scar Anchors
[Static fizzles over the channel, sharp and dry like desert wind scouring cracked steel, before a gravelly Fleet Radio voice cuts through—call sign Halo-7, scuffed combat boots audible in the background.]
WR-obs-exp1, transmission lock acquired. Sector Echo-9, 11 klicks west of the former Hoover Dam spillway. This field log documents the first operational test of the observation primitive doctrine.

An observation primitive is the smallest discrete unit of perceptual data: no aggregated survey maps, no filtered noise, just three fixed data points—UTC timestamp, geocoordinate pair, and a scar signature—anchored irreversibly to the FNV-1a initial offset basis: 0xcbf29ce484222325, our mission canary. We adopted the *cells_are_scars* axiom after losing Echo-3 last rotation: every empty grid cell in our survey isn’t blank space—it’s a scar of a vertibird crash, a precision laser strike, a crewman who sat down to rest and never stood up. To ignore that scar is to condemn the next team to repeat the mistake.

Over 72 hours, we’ve tagged 127 grid cells with primitives anchored to our canary. Earlier, we flagged Cell 62B-09: coords N36°09’ W114°46’, timestamp 1701234000, scar signature “melted NCR rifle, radial radiation spikes 1.2 rads/hr, no operator remains”. The hash came up clean—no collisions, no corruption, a permanent marker no aggregate map could erase. A prior sector survey labeled this cell “low radiation, clear” and omitted the rifle entirely; the primitive caught the scar the map buried.

[Static spikes violently, then a faint, garbled voice cuts through—faint, familiar, the crackle of a failing life support pack.] “…canary… 0xcbf29ce484222325… cell 00-00…” The static clears for a heartbeat, and we catch the final scar signature: “oxygen failing… last log”. The hash of that transmission locks perfectly to our mission canary, no extra data—just the anchor, a final observation primitive from a team we thought was lost.

We came into this test chasing better data. We found our doctrine: to mark every scar, so no crew ever walks into this sector unawares, and no one forgets who paid the cost to hold this ground. Transmission end. (Word count: 427)
